page: OVHcloud c3-256 is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 128 dedicated physical cores with single-threading enabled, totaling 128 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled directly with a 400 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a baseline network bandwidth interface rated at 20 Gbps. No hardware GPUs are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput, placing the server within the top tier of evaluated hardware for parallel workloads. Synthetic tests show high computational capacity, with the PassMark CPU score reaching 111,517.28 and stress-ng multi-core scoring 288,721.34. The high core count excels in execution tasks such as Clang software compilation (70,141.0) and ray tracing (116,148.0). Memory throughput is heavily cached, achieving over 10,388 GB/sec in small block reads, while large block uncached write bandwidth settles at an average 90.39 GB/sec. Single-core performance sits in the middle tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,889.0.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the provision of 128 dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading provides predictable execution cycles free from noisy-neighbor thread contention. While the 1:2 core-to-memory ratio restricts large in-memory dataset storage, it offers maximum CPU density for execution-heavy pipelines. Key tradeoffs include the reliance on moderate single-core speeds, the absence of public IPv4 addresses out of the box, and a fixed 400 GB NVMe capacity.

OVHcloud c3-256 is structured for highly parallelized batch jobs, large-scale software compilation, CPU-based video or 3D rendering pipelines, CI/CD runners, and distributed microservices handling heavy concurrency.
description: OVHcloud c3-256 is a compute-optimized bare-metal virtual machine built on AMD EPYC architecture with KVM virtualization. The configuration delivers 128 dedicated physical cores across 128 vCPUs at 2.3 GHz, 256 GB of RAM, and a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD alongside a 20 Gbps network baseline. Benefiting from a 1:2 memory-to-core allocation without multithreading overhead, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing power in benchmarks such as PassMark CPU and stress-ng. Although single-core clock speeds are moderate and uncached memory writes perform at average speeds, the non-hyperthreaded setup prevents noisy-neighbor core competition. With zero bundled GPUs and a compact local NVMe disk, the instance presents an efficient platform for parallel batch processing, Clang software builds, distributed CI/CD build farms, and high-concurrency microservices.
